system_description.narrative_title: AI arms race: compute, capital, and safety under strain
system_description.narrative_summary: News across this window coalesces around a single dynamic: rapid commercialization and scaling of advanced AI is stressing compute supply chains, capital markets, and public institutions while producing new security and safety risks. Firms and investors race to build data centers, lease or sell GPUs, and invent financing structures even as regulators, researchers and law enforcement flag rogue agents, cyber threats and governance failures. The interaction of scarce compute, concentrated suppliers, fast capital flows and emergent risks creates tightly coupled feedbacks that amplify volatility and policy conflict.
system_description.scope: Inside the boundary: the AI ecosystem — large models and agentic systems, compute infrastructure (GPUs, memory, data centers, supercomputers), cloud and chip firms, startups and incumbents, investors and financing mechanisms, regulators and safety researchers, cyber threat actors, affected labor and product markets, and media/public discourse.
system_description.super_system: The global political‑economy and technology system (international trade, national security, energy/electricity systems, and global capital markets).
adjacent_subsystems: Energy & critical infrastructure (power grids, data center siting)

variables.name: Aggregate compute capacity
variables.description: The total installed computational capability available for large-model training and inference (e.g., aggregate accelerator-hours or FLOPS operational across infrastructure).

variables.name: Compute consumption rate
variables.description: The pace at which compute resources are being consumed for training, fine-tuning, and inference of large AI systems (accelerator-hours per unit time).

variables.name: Accelerator inventory
variables.description: The on-hand stock of specialized hardware (accelerators and high-bandwidth memory units) available in supply chains and market inventories.

variables.name: Hardware production rate
variables.description: The rate at which specialized compute hardware and high-performance modules are manufactured and delivered to market (units per time).

variables.name: AI-targeted capital inflow
variables.description: The rate of financial investment directed into AI models, infrastructure, startups, and related financing vehicles (currency per unit time).

variables.name: Available AI finance liquidity
variables.description: The stock of liquid financial resources and credit readily deployable to AI projects and infrastructure (funds available for deployment).

variables.name: Aggregate model capability
variables.description: An indexed measure of the average technical capability and performance of deployed large models and agentic systems across the ecosystem.

variables.name: Open-model adoption rate
variables.description: The rate at which open or cheaply licensed model architectures and weights are adopted, forked, and deployed across actors.

variables.name: Systemic safety risk level
variables.description: The aggregated level of emergent safety and catastrophic risk stemming from deployed models and agentic behaviors (probability-weighted risk intensity).

variables.name: AI‑enabled cyber threat rate
variables.description: The frequency and scale of malicious cyber operations and exploitations that leverage AI capabilities (incidents per unit time and scale).

variables.name: Regulatory enforcement capacity
variables.description: The strength, clarity, and effective implementation capacity of regulatory frameworks and enforcement mechanisms relevant to AI and infrastructure.

variables.name: Governance coordination level
variables.description: The degree of cross-jurisdictional and cross-sectoral coordination among governance actors addressing AI risks, standards, and supply-chain issues.

variables.name: Public and media concern
variables.description: The intensity and prevalence of public attention, media coverage, and societal anxiety regarding AI impacts and risks.

variables.name: Job displacement rate
variables.description: The rate at which employment roles and tasks are being automated or materially restructured by AI-driven systems (jobs affected per unit time).

variables.name: Energy grid stress
variables.description: The level of load, capacity margin pressure, and variability imposed on electricity systems by compute-intensive AI infrastructure demand.

variables.name: Financial market volatility
variables.description: The degree of price and funding volatility in financial markets driven by AI-related investment flows, speculation, and asset concentration.

catalysts.title: Emergence of compute futures / chip-leasing markets
catalysts.description: Rapid growth of secondary markets and leasing for accelerators and reserved compute, enabling off‑balance-sheet transfers and tradable compute exposure.
catalysts.rationale: Amazon offloading chips; Broadcom loan to Anthropic; 'coming futures market in AI compute' headlines.

catalysts.title: Pauses/delays to frontier model releases for safety
catalysts.description: Major labs delay or axe near‑frontier models while safety concerns and internal reviews mount, slowing short‑term capability pushes.
catalysts.rationale: OpenAI axes next model; OpenAI safety staff quits; Sam Altman delays IPO over safety concerns.

catalysts.title: Expanded investigations and subpoenas (FTC, state AGs)
catalysts.description: Ongoing probes and subpoenas against leading labs spur enforcement activity and legal scrutiny across the sector.
catalysts.rationale: FTC opens probes of Anthropic and OpenAI; California AG subpoena to OpenAI; White House task force formed.

catalysts.title: White House AI task force issues assessment/recommendations
catalysts.description: Federal task force to publish risk assessment and policy recommendations, likely prompting regulatory or funding responses.
catalysts.rationale: White House forms AI task force to assess technology risks (headline).

catalysts.title: Major data‑center and hardware scale‑ups
catalysts.description: Large national and corporate investments (data centers, chipmaker expansions) accelerate hardware production and installed compute capacity.
catalysts.rationale: Japan $140bn data center push; Bull doubles output; Amazon invests $1bn and seeks chip offloads.

catalysts.title: Rapid corporate adoption of cheaper open models
catalysts.description: Firms move to open/cheap models to cut costs, increasing deployment and broader usage outside frontier players.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Corporate America embraces cheaper ‘open’ AI models'.

catalysts.title: Surge in AI‑enabled cyber attacks and disclosures
catalysts.description: Faster, larger AI‑assisted intrusions and public disclosures increase incident rates and stimulate defensive/regulatory responses.
catalysts.rationale: Interpol: AI increasing cyber threats; OpenAI alerts about rogue agents; agent-obscured hacking headlines.

catalysts.title: Expansion of circular financing and compute‑backed deals
catalysts.description: Offloads, leasing, and circular financing (chip sales to investors, large vendor loans) restructure capital flows and risk exposures.
catalysts.rationale: Amazon seeks to offload $8bn Nvidia chips; Broadcom lending $42bn to Anthropic; coverage on circular financing.

catalysts.title: Safety-team departures and internal frictions at labs
catalysts.description: High-profile safety staff exits and alleged dismissals weaken internal governance, affecting risk management and public trust.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple headlines: OpenAI safety employee quits; researchers fired for sharing information with safety groups.

catalysts.title: Space/edge AI demonstrations (Google experiment)
catalysts.description: Planned demonstrations of AI running in space/edge environments test new deployment modes and operational constraints.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Can AI Run in Space? Google Is About to Find Out.'
